name: Compiler Flag Explainer
blurb: size and speed effect of the optimisation flags in a build log
intro: Reads GCC/Clang flags out of a pasted build log or CFLAGS/LDFLAGS and says, for each one, which way it moves code size and speed and why, from the GCC manual. It flags mixed -O levels, section flags without --gc-sections, fast-math and float-ABI mistakes, and lists what is missing for a size, speed or debug build.

inputs.label: Build log or flags
inputs.default:
arm-none-eabi-gcc -mcpu=cortex-m4 -mthumb -mfpu=fpv4-sp-d16 -mfloat-abi=hard -O2 -g3 -Wall -Wextra -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections -DSTM32F411xE -DUSE_HAL_DRIVER -IInc -c Src/main.c -o build/main.o
arm-none-eabi-gcc -mcpu=cortex-m4 -mthumb -mfpu=fpv4-sp-d16 -mfloat-abi=hard -O0 -g3 -Wall -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections -c Src/stm32f4xx_it.c -o build/stm32f4xx_it.o
arm-none-eabi-gcc build/main.o build/stm32f4xx_it.o -mcpu=cortex-m4 -mthumb -mfpu=fpv4-sp-d16 -mfloat-abi=hard --specs=nano.specs -u _printf_float -TSTM32F411RETx_FLASH.ld -Wl,-Map=build/app.map,--cref -o build/app.elf
inputs.help: make V=1, ninja -v, or compile_commands.json output; one command per line.

examples.title: STM32 Makefile build aimed at small flash

input.log:
arm-none-eabi-gcc -mcpu=cortex-m4 -mthumb -mfpu=fpv4-sp-d16 -mfloat-abi=hard -O2 -g3 -Wall -Wextra -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections -DSTM32F411xE -DUSE_HAL_DRIVER -IInc -c Src/main.c -o build/main.o
arm-none-eabi-gcc -mcpu=cortex-m4 -mthumb -mfpu=fpv4-sp-d16 -mfloat-abi=hard -O0 -g3 -Wall -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections -c Src/stm32f4xx_it.c -o build/stm32f4xx_it.o
arm-none-eabi-gcc build/main.o build/stm32f4xx_it.o -mcpu=cortex-m4 -mthumb -mfpu=fpv4-sp-d16 -mfloat-abi=hard --specs=nano.specs -u _printf_float -TSTM32F411RETx_FLASH.ld -Wl,-Map=build/app.map,--cref -o build/app.elf

examples.title: Host C++ build aimed at speed

input.log:
g++ -std=c++17 -O3 -ffast-math -march=native -flto -fno-exceptions -Wall -c dsp.cpp -o dsp.o
g++ -O3 -flto dsp.o -o dsp

usage: Give the build log text (one compiler or linker command per line, or plain CFLAGS/LDFLAGS) and the goal (size, speed or debug). It returns the dominant -O level, a table of every recognised flag with its size and speed direction and a one-line explanation, the flags worth adding for the goal, warnings about mixed or conflicting flags, and a Flags text with a suggested set. Use it to explain why a firmware image is large or slow, or to review a build configuration.
sources: GCC manual, 'Options That Control Optimization', 'Options for Code Generation Conventions', 'ARM Options', 'Options for Linking' (gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs)
